# LatencyGuard

[![Last Commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/Kkthnx-Wow/LatencyGuard)](https://github.com/Kkthnx-Wow/LatencyGuard/commits/main)
[![Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/Kkthnx-Wow/LatencyGuard)](https://github.com/Kkthnx-Wow/LatencyGuard/issues)
[![CurseForge](https://img.shields.io/badge/CurseForge-Download-orange)](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/latency-guard)

Keeps your Spell Queue Window matched to your connection and shows you what that connection is doing. For World of Warcraft Retail and WoW Forever.

## Why it matters

The Spell Queue Window lets you press your next ability a little before the current cast or global cooldown ends, so it fires with no gap. The game default is 400ms for everyone. On a 30ms connection that commits you to your next press far too early, which makes reacting to procs and interrupts harder. On an unstable connection a window that is too small drops presses. LatencyGuard sets it for you and keeps it right as your connection changes.

## What it does

- Sets the window to your world latency plus a safety margin, kept between 100 and 400ms.
- Uses a separate, tighter margin in arenas and battlegrounds if you want one.
- Adds headroom when your latency readings are uneven, up to 150ms.
- Widens at once when needed and waits 45 seconds before narrowing, so a short calm does not remove protection right before the next spike.
- Changes the setting only out of combat.
- Steps aside for 10 minutes when another addon, a macro or the console changes the window, instead of fighting over it.
- Puts back your own value when you turn automation off.

## What it shows

- An optional movable readout with world latency, frame rate and the current Spell Queue Window. Hover it for the full report. While hidden it does no work at all.
- A live report on its options page and through `/latencyguard status`. It covers world and home latency, latency range and spread, bandwidth, frame rate with average and low, the target and how it was worked out, and your Low Latency Mode setting.
- An optional chat alert when world latency spikes past a threshold you choose, and another when it settles.
- A data broker feed for broker bars and data texts.

The game refreshes its latency figure about every 30 seconds, so everything above moves at that pace. LatencyGuard does not invent faster numbers.

## Install

Install from [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/latency-guard), or download the latest zip from [Releases](https://github.com/Kkthnx-Wow/LatencyGuard/releases) and extract the `LatencyGuard` folder into your AddOns folder.

- Retail: `World of Warcraft/_retail_/Interface/AddOns`
- WoW Forever: `World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns`

## Use

It works as soon as you log in. Open the options with `/latencyguard` or `/latguard`.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/latencyguard` | Open the options |
| `/latencyguard status` | Print the live report |
| `/latencyguard readout` | Show or hide the readout |
| `/latencyguard resume` | End a pause caused by an outside change |
| `/latencyguard restore` | Turn automation off and put back your own value |
| `/latencyguard reset` | Clear latency and frame rate samples |

Suggested safety margins are 30 to 70ms for reactive PvP, 70 to 130ms for most play and 100 to 150ms for steady PvE.

## Development

The addon is plain Lua 5.1 with no build step. Before a release:

```
luacheck .
lua5.1 tests/run.lua
lua5.1 tests/run.lua . fresh
```

The tests load every file in TOC order against a stubbed game API and drive events, timers and settings. They check logic, not in-game behavior.

To release, set `## Version` in `LatencyGuard.toc`, commit, then push an annotated tag with the same number. The release workflow lints, tests, packages and uploads to GitHub Releases and CurseForge.

```
git tag -a 3.0.0 -m "3.0.0"
git push origin 3.0.0
```

# LatencyGuard

## [3.0.0](https://github.com/Kkthnx-Wow/LatencyGuard/tree/3.0.0) (2026-11-25)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/Kkthnx-Wow/LatencyGuard/commits/3.0.0) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/Kkthnx-Wow/LatencyGuard/releases)

- Add a tag-driven release workflow, lint and tests, and rewrite the README  
    Pushing an annotated tag lints with luacheck, runs the behaviour tests,  
    then packages one zip tagged for Retail and Forever and uploads it to  
    GitHub Releases and CurseForge. The README covers what 3.0 does, the  
    commands and how to cut a release, and fixes the CurseForge link.  
- Rebuild LatencyGuard 3.0 for Retail and Forever  
    Tune the Spell Queue Window from measured world latency, a safety  
    margin and headroom from latency spread. Widen at once, wait before  
    narrowing, write only out of combat, step aside after an outside change  
    and restore the player's own value when turned off.  
    Add a movable readout, a live report on the options page and in  
    /latencyguard status, a latency spike alert and a data broker feed with  
    bundled LibStub, CallbackHandler-1.0 and LibDataBroker-1.1. Move the  
    addon to the repository root, replace the icon, and carry 2.x settings  
    over to an account-wide layout.  
- Add FUNDING.yml  
- Standardize README  
- Update README.md  
- Add adaptive jitter and diagnostic status command  
    Refactors network logic into a dedicated Network.lua module and implements adaptive jitter-aware margin calculation. Adds `/latencyguard status` command for comprehensive diagnostics. Changes primary slash command from `/lg` to `/latencyguard` (with `/latguard` alias) to avoid conflicts with other addons. Improves landing page UI, adds database value sanitization, and enhances localization with new diagnostic strings.  
- Merge branch 'main' of https://github.com/Kkthnx-Wow/LatencyGuard  
- Refactor core into modular framework  
    Replace the legacy flat core/config with a modular engine and reorganized code. Removed old Config.lua, Core.lua, Logic.lua and top-level Locales; added Core/{Engine,Database,Functions,Constants,Commands} and Core/Locales/* plus Modules/SpellQueue. Introduces a module registry, centralized event dispatcher and internal signal bus, a lightweight profile-based DB with migration to schema v1, utility helpers, and an options/commands builder (slash /lg and Settings panel). Updated TOC to match the new layout. This modernizes the addon architecture, enables per-profile settings and live module setting updates.  
- Fix CurseForge link in README.md  
- Guard Secret Values, bump version, refresh docs  
    Add a defensive fallback for Midnight's Secret Values (issecretvalue) and skip UpdateQueueWindow when GetNetStats returns a secreted latency to avoid Lua errors on 12.0+ clients. Bump TOC version to 2.0.4 and simplify Interface line. Remove the addon-level README and replace/update the repository README with an expanded, polished documentation and install/usage guide.  
- Add locales and refactor core/config/logic  
    Add full i18n support (enUS + 12 locale files) and register them in the TOC; bump addon version and interface entries. Replace legacy InterfaceOptions UI with the Settings API canvas/subcategory/proxy settings in Config.lua, including localized strings and improved layout. Refactor Core.lua to introduce a centralized event dispatcher (NS:RegisterEvent/UnregisterEvent), auto-initialize modules on ADDON\_LOADED, and localize startup messages; improve slash command registration to use ADDON\_NAME. Simplify Logic.lua timers and discovery flow (discoveryActive, named callbacks), register PLAYER\_REGEN\_ENABLED via the new event system, and clean up ticker callbacks and localized update messages. Overall: modernization, localization, and cleaner event/timer handling.  
- Replace icon file with TGA format  
    Removed LatencyGuard\_Icon.blp and added LatencyGuard\_Icon.tga to update the icon format.  
- Revise README for improved clarity and structure  
    Updated README to enhance clarity and organization, including feature descriptions and usage instructions.  
- Refactor LatencyGuard to modular structure  
    Reorganized the addon by removing legacy core, event, helper, command, and settings modules, and introduced new modular files: Core.lua, Logic.lua, and Config.lua. Updated the TOC to reflect the new structure, removed unused libraries and localization files, and simplified the configuration and initialization logic. This refactor streamlines the codebase for maintainability and future development.  
- Refactor into modular architecture and add core modules  
    Split LatencyGuard into modular components: Helpers, Engine, Events, and Commands, each in its own file for maintainability and clarity. Updated main LatencyGuard.lua to handle only constants, state, and option callback registration. Enhanced documentation, improved timer and event handling, and added a README. Updated .toc for new version, module order, and metadata. Default enableGuard is now true.  
- Big refactor.  
- Update README.md  
- Reworked the entire addon.  
- Update README.md  
- 🎉 Release: LatencyGuard v1.0 - Dynamic Latency Optimization  
    🚀 We're excited to announce the release of LatencyGuard v1.0! This version marks a significant milestone in providing a seamless and optimized gameplay experience for World of Warcraft players.  
    🌟 Key Features:  
    - 📶 Dynamic Spell Queue Window Adjustment: Automatically adapts to current network latency for optimal performance.  
    - 🎚️ User-Controlled Settings: Customizable latency threshold and feedback options.  
    - 💾 Persistent Configuration: Settings are saved and retained across game sessions.  
    - 📈 Enhanced Gameplay: Reduced lag impact, ensuring smoother and more responsive gameplay.  
    🔍 This release has undergone thorough testing to ensure reliability and performance. We're committed to continuous improvement and eagerly await your feedback.  
    🙌 A big thank you to our community for your support and suggestions. Enjoy the enhanced gaming experience with LatencyGuard v1.0!
